question: Which L2 strength lambda provides the lowest 5-fold cross-validated Brier score?
rationale: Full-batch gradient descent with 200 iterations and clip logits to [-30, 30]. Standard 5-fold contiguous block cross-validation on data splits. Brier score is computed per fold and averaged. The lambda value producing minimum CV Brier is selected.
decision: Fit logistic regression with each lambda value in [0.0, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0] using exact fitting conventions (200 iters, lr=0.1, clipping). Select lambda with minimum mean 5-fold Brier.
expected_effect: Identification of optimal L2 strength; typical improvement ranges 1-5% over no regularization depending on data characteristics. Risk: if all lambdas perform similarly, improvement_over_baseline may be near zero.
falsifier: If no lambda improves over baseline (lambda=0), improvement_over_baseline will be reported as ≤0, and any lambda value may be reported as best_lambda.

question: Do interaction features statistically improve model performance at lambda=0.1?
alternatives: Add interaction features x0*x1, x1*x2, x2*x3, x0*x3
rationale: Fit two models: (1) raw features only, (2) raw + 4 interaction features. Both use lambda=0.1, same GD conventions. Paired t-test compares Brier scores per fold. t > 2.0 indicates statistically significant improvement.
decision: Fit both models with lambda=0.1 across 5 folds. Compute paired t-test (raw - interaction Brier per fold). interaction_helps = True iff t-statistic > 2.0.
expected_effect: If interactions correlate with label, t-statistic will be positive and potentially > 2.0. If interactions hurt or add noise, t will be negative or near zero. Risk: small sample size (5 folds) makes significance testing sensitive to outliers.
falsifier: If computed t-statistic ≤ 2.0, interaction_helps = False, regardless of sign. If t > 2.0, interaction_helps = True.

question: Which model compression config (sparsity %, bit precision) retains the most dense-model performance?
rationale: Fit dense model on all rows with lambda=0.1. For each (sparsity%, bits) config: zero smallest-magnitude weights (k=round(p*d)), quantize remaining weights uniformly onto 2^bits levels between min/max. Compute in-sample Brier for compressed model. Retention = dense_brier / compressed_brier. Highest retention config is best.
decision: Fit dense model once. Apply 6 compression configs. Compute in-sample Brier for each. Select config with maximum retention ratio.
expected_effect: Retention will decrease as sparsity and bit precision increase (more aggressive compression). Lower sparsity and higher bit precision typically retain more performance. Risk: retention ratio inversion if dense model has high variance; quantization artifacts may dominate at ultra-low precision.
falsifier: Config with lowest retention is explicitly rejected. Config with highest retention (≥1.0 or close) is selected regardless of sparsity/bits values.
